purpose: Candidate small/fast model architectures, RL approaches, and inference runtimes considered for the two bespoke-model roles in Garment Pattern Lab's DAG spine: (V-Model) raster-to-tagged-vector vectorization+semantic interpretation, and (R-Model) iterative pattern refinement against the validation gate. Read in companion with docs/research/bespoke-model-opportunities-2026-05-03.md.

field_definitions.id: Stable kebab-case identifier for the candidate.
field_definitions.name: Display name.
field_definitions.family: One of: vision-encoder, vision-decoder, set-transformer, sketch-gnn, structured-vector-decoder, tiny-lm, ssm, distillation-method, quantization-method, lora-method, runtime, rl-algorithm, search-policy, verifier-pattern, dataset-method, prior-art-system.
field_definitions.url: Primary reference URL (paper, project page, or repo).
field_definitions.role_applicability: Which bespoke-model role(s) the candidate applies to: vectorization | refinement | both | infrastructure | training-only.
field_definitions.size_class: tiny<100M | small<1B | medium<10B | large | not-applicable. For training/RL methods, this names the size class typically targeted.
field_definitions.license: Headline license. SPDX-style or descriptive. null if unknown.
field_definitions.training_data_requirements: Free-form note on what labeled / paired / verifier data is required for the candidate to be useful.
field_definitions.browser_deployable: yes | no | partial | via-distillation | via-port. Whether the candidate runs in a browser today as the user would experience it.
field_definitions.inference_speed_class: instant<10ms | fast<50ms | medium<200ms | slow<1s | very-slow>1s | not-applicable. Targeted at v0.2-v1 model sizes on M-series Mac with WebGPU; coarse.
field_definitions.rl_ready: yes | no | partial | n/a. Whether the candidate is suitable as the policy/value/training-target in a verifier-rewarded RL loop.
field_definitions.applicability_score: 1-5; 5 = directly recommended for v0.2 or v0.5; 1 = research-only/excluded.
field_definitions.applicability_rationale: One-paragraph rationale tied to Pattern Lab constraints.
field_definitions.staging: v0.2 | v0.5 | v1 | v1.5 | research-only | excluded.

candidates.name: MobileSAM (image encoder, ViT-Tiny)
candidates.training_data_requirements: Pretrained on SAM corpus; for our use it is a frozen feature extractor. Fine-tuning is optional and would need ~10k garment-sketch images.
candidates.applicability_rationale: Smallest viable image encoder with strong sketch transferability and a clean ONNX path. ~6MB FP16 bundle, ~10ms WebGPU inference. Recommended V-Model trunk for v0.2.
candidates.notes: Use only the image encoder portion (~5.78MB). Discard the prompt decoder; replace with our Set Transformer curve decoder.

candidates.name: MobileViT v2
candidates.training_data_requirements: ImageNet-pretrained checkpoints available; for sketches consider domain fine-tuning on synthetic line-rendered garments.
candidates.applicability_rationale: Strong alternative to MobileSAM if MobileSAM's SAM-distilled features prove poorly suited to clean line art. Slightly larger but still browser-trivial.
candidates.notes: Trade vs MobileSAM: MobileSAM is segmentation-trained (likely better at object/shape grounding); MobileViT is classification-trained (likely better at style/texture). Run a small bake-off.

candidates.name: FastSAM
candidates.training_data_requirements: Pretrained on SA-1B; license is AGPL which is a real product concern.
candidates.applicability_rationale: Faster than vanilla SAM but larger than MobileSAM and AGPL-licensed; the latter is a hard product blocker for a closed deployment.
candidates.notes: Useful as a research baseline; not a deployment candidate.

candidates.name: Set Transformer
candidates.training_data_requirements: Per-curve role labels; works with synthetic-from-FreeSewing labels and/or distillation-from-multimodal-LLM labels.
candidates.applicability_rationale: Permutation-invariant attention exactly matches the inductive bias for unordered-curve tagging. 4 layers / 128 dim / 4 heads ~1.5M params, trivial to ship via ONNX.
candidates.notes: Recommended V-Model decoder. Output: per-curve role logits + endpoint refinement deltas.

candidates.name: SketchGNN
candidates.training_data_requirements: Per-stroke labels with adjacency; we'd build adjacency from endpoint sharing.
candidates.applicability_rationale: Right structural shape, but adds graph construction overhead vs Set Transformer. Better choice if curve-curve adjacency matters strongly (it might for darts/seam pairs); worth a v0.5 bake-off.
candidates.notes: Compare against Set Transformer once a real correction corpus exists. May win on dart-vs-style-line discrimination.

candidates.name: DeepSVG
candidates.training_data_requirements: SVG-token sequences with role labels; can be generated from FreeSewing/GarmentCode parameter sweeps.
candidates.applicability_rationale: Gives a clean SVG-command output vocabulary that drops directly into our existing curve schema. Original is 12+12 layers; a 4+4 distillation should fit comfortably under 100M params.
candidates.notes: Use as an output-representation lesson rather than as the full architecture for v0.2.

candidates.name: BezierSketch
candidates.training_data_requirements: Raster + Bezier-stroke pairs. Limited public corpus; would need synthetic generation.
candidates.applicability_rationale: Useful inspiration for raster->Bezier learning, but our V-Model uses classical tracers as the curve proposer, so BezierSketch's contribution is partially redundant.
candidates.notes: Revisit if classical tracers prove inadequate on hand-drawn sketches.

candidates.name: SmolLM2-135M-Instruct
candidates.training_data_requirements: QLoRA fine-tune on synthetic operation traces (~50-100k per family). DPO/GRPO on real correction logs in v1.
candidates.applicability_rationale: Smallest credible LLM that can emit structured JSON operations. ~70MB at 4-bit GGUF, runs in WebLLM/wllama. Recommended R-Model base for v0.5.
candidates.notes: Benchmark with project-shape prompts before committing; the ~200ms/step assumption is extrapolated, not measured.

candidates.name: Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct
candidates.training_data_requirements: Same as SmolLM2; Qwen has slightly stronger reasoning baseline so may need less fine-tune data.
candidates.applicability_rationale: Step up from SmolLM2-135M (~3.7x params) with better instruction-following; ~280MB at 4-bit GGUF. Use if SmolLM2-135M underperforms on operation-emission accuracy.
candidates.notes: Ships with a usable instruction-tuned baseline; less fine-tune data needed than SmolLM2.

candidates.name: Gemma 3 270M
candidates.training_data_requirements: Marketed by Google as fine-tune-friendly; recipe expectations similar to SmolLM2/Qwen.
candidates.applicability_rationale: Promising recent option (Aug 2025). Gemma license is permissive but not OSI-Apache; needs legal review before committing.
candidates.notes: Lawful redistribution within product needs explicit license review against Gemma terms before adoption.

candidates.name: Phi-3-mini
candidates.training_data_requirements: Strong instruction baseline; QLoRA on operation traces.
candidates.applicability_rationale: Too large for a target browser inference budget on most hardware (~2.4GB at 4-bit). Use server-side as a teacher for distillation; not as the deployed R-Model.
candidates.notes: Could host as a server-side teacher; per-token latency on the browser exceeds the interactive budget.

candidates.name: RWKV (tiny via web-rwkv)
candidates.training_data_requirements: Same fine-tune corpus as SmolLM2.
candidates.applicability_rationale: Linear-time SSM with a working browser runtime, but the operation-token sequences in our use case are short enough that attention's quadratic cost is negligible. The SSM advantage isn't load-bearing here.
candidates.notes: Revisit if multi-step planning sequences blow past 4k tokens.

candidates.name: Mamba
candidates.training_data_requirements: Same as Qwen for fine-tuning; pretrained checkpoints in 130M-2.8B sizes.
candidates.applicability_rationale: Hardware-aware selective scan kernel does not yet have a clean WebGPU implementation. Server-side only for now.
candidates.notes: Track WebGPU port progress; not on a deployment path in 2026-05.

candidates.name: LoRA (low-rank adapters)
candidates.training_data_requirements: Per-task labeled data; for us, per-garment-family corpora.
candidates.applicability_rationale: Default fine-tune method. Per-family adapters at rank 8-16 add 1-4M params, swappable at runtime, near-zero inference overhead.
candidates.notes: Use with frozen base for both V-Model and R-Model. Calibrate rank in a v0.5 spike.

candidates.name: QLoRA
candidates.training_data_requirements: Same as LoRA.
candidates.applicability_rationale: QLoRA on a 4-bit-quantized base lets us fine-tune SmolLM2-135M / Qwen-0.5B on a single consumer GPU. Required for the per-family training plan.
candidates.notes: Pair with deepspeed/bitsandbytes on the training side; inference unchanged from LoRA.

candidates.name: INT8 / INT4 quantization (ONNX)
candidates.training_data_requirements: Calibration set of ~512-1024 representative inputs.
candidates.applicability_rationale: Default V-Model deployment quantization. Quality degradation typically <1% on classification heads; tolerable on regression heads with calibration.
candidates.notes: Profile both per-tensor and per-channel quantization for the Set Transformer head.

candidates.name: GGML / GGUF Q4_K_M quantization
candidates.training_data_requirements: n/a
candidates.applicability_rationale: Standard quantization for browser-side LLM inference via wllama / WebLLM. ~3.5-4x model size reduction with marginal quality loss.
candidates.notes: WebLLM uses MLC-AI quantization formats; wllama uses GGUF. Choose based on chosen runtime.

candidates.name: Distillation from multimodal LLM (GPT-4o / Claude)
candidates.training_data_requirements: Teacher API access + corpus of unlabeled sketches with consent for training use.
candidates.applicability_rationale: Cheap labeling for v0.5 supervised stage. Filter teacher outputs through the validation gate to drop hallucinations.
candidates.notes: Consent and IP handling per InputProvenance is required before any user uploads can be sent to teachers.

candidates.name: Synthetic dataset generation from FreeSewing parameter sweeps
candidates.training_data_requirements: FreeSewing source code (already a project dependency); compute for parameter sweeps.
candidates.applicability_rationale: Cleanest synthetic-data generator we have. Ground truth comes for free; perturbation + heuristic-refine produces R-Model trajectories.
candidates.notes: Need a perturbation-distribution calibration spike before scaling. Listed as a known gap in the reference doc.

candidates.name: GarmentCodeData
candidates.training_data_requirements: Public dataset (~1k procedurally generated patterns) plus the GarmentCode authoring DSL.
candidates.applicability_rationale: Out-of-distribution evaluation set first; training set later if license review clears commercial use. Conversion shim into our PatternGraph schema needs ~1 day.
candidates.notes: Verify license terms for product use before training-set adoption.

candidates.name: SewFactory
candidates.training_data_requirements: Public dataset (~13k pattern + drape pairs).
candidates.applicability_rationale: Larger but research-licensed; research-evaluation use only without explicit relicensing.
candidates.notes: Useful for V-Model OOD evaluation and SewFormer-style ablations.

candidates.name: Iterative refinement (AlphaFold-shape)
candidates.training_data_requirements: n/a (architectural pattern).
candidates.applicability_rationale: Direct architectural fit for the R-Model: small model called many times beats big model called once. AlphaFold's structure module runs the same block 8x; our R-Model should run 8-12 inner steps per refinement call.
candidates.notes: Iteration count is a hyperparameter, not learned. Stop on gate-pass, on budget, or on plateau.

candidates.name: Diffusion / Flow Matching
candidates.training_data_requirements: Pairs of (noisy, clean) candidates; can be synthesized from gate-passing patterns by perturbation.
candidates.applicability_rationale: Conceptually right: denoising = repeatedly nudging a candidate toward the data distribution. Overkill at v0.5; credible v1 architecture if operation-trace corpus is large enough.
candidates.notes: Use with a learned surrogate of the gate to enable verifier-guided sampling, since the gate itself isn't differentiable.

candidates.name: MuZero-shape value head + tree search
candidates.training_data_requirements: Trajectories of (state, eventual gate-pass distance) pairs; cannot build until R-Model v0.5 has logged thousands of trajectories.
candidates.applicability_rationale: Endgame R-Model architecture: action proposer + value head + MCTS. Premature for v0.5; right shape for v1.5.
candidates.notes: Value head is a small MLP over state-features predicting probability of gate-pass within K steps.

candidates.name: Best-of-N inference
candidates.training_data_requirements: n/a.
candidates.applicability_rationale: Trivial to implement and surprisingly strong. With N=4-8 and a 100ms model, a refinement step is 400-800ms; fits an interactive budget.
candidates.notes: Score with the real gate at the operation level; don't bother training a separate scorer in v0.5.

candidates.name: Process Reward Model (PRM)
candidates.training_data_requirements: Per-step labels of "on-track to pass" / "off-track". Can be generated from synthetic trajectories.
candidates.applicability_rationale: Useful when we want beam search / best-of-N at every inner-loop step rather than only the outer. Pays off at v1+ scale.
candidates.notes: Train a small MLP over diagnostics + state features.

candidates.name: PPO
candidates.training_data_requirements: Online interaction with the verifier; replay buffer; value-function training data.
candidates.applicability_rationale: Workhorse algorithm but value-function training adds complexity; GRPO is a leaner choice for our small-model setup.
candidates.notes: Default fallback if GRPO underperforms.

candidates.name: DPO (Direct Preference Optimization)
candidates.training_data_requirements: (preferred, dispreferred) pairs. Cheap to source from the gate (pick the candidate it prefers) and from the manual correction log (user-corrected vs heuristic-original).
candidates.applicability_rationale: Cheapest first move for verifier-rewarded fine-tune. Avoids reward-hacking pathologies of full PPO.
candidates.notes: Use over the IntelligenceLearningLoop correction corpus.

candidates.name: GRPO (Group-Relative Policy Optimization)
candidates.training_data_requirements: Online verifier interaction; group-of-N rollouts per prompt.
candidates.applicability_rationale: No value function needed (matters for tiny base models). DeepSeek-R1 / Qwen-reasoning evidence shows it works at our scale. Default v1 RL choice.
candidates.notes: Group size 8 fits a single workstation training step.

candidates.name: RLAIF / RLAF
candidates.training_data_requirements: AI feedback (large model as judge) when ground-truth is unavailable.
candidates.applicability_rationale: Useful when the gate is silent on a quality dimension we care about (e.g. design coherence). For most of our use cases the gate is enough.
candidates.notes: Hybrid with verifier-RL: gate as the binary reward, AI feedback as the soft signal.

candidates.name: Self-play / AlphaZero shape
candidates.training_data_requirements: Self-generated problems: model perturbs valid patterns and learns to refine them back.
candidates.applicability_rationale: Free training data once a stable validator and forward model exist. Pattern Lab has both. Right shape for v1+.
candidates.notes: Combine with curriculum (start with easy garments, unlock harder).

candidates.name: Component-weighted reward shaping
candidates.training_data_requirements: Existing validation rule outputs; weight tuning needs patternmaker review.
candidates.applicability_rationale: The gate already emits per-rule diagnostics. -Sigma weight_i * normalized_error_i + bonus_pass turns sparse pass/fail into dense signal. Required for stable RL.
candidates.notes: Initial weights = 1 across rules. Patternmaker reviews the weights at the v1 checkpoint (Orrery review finding 15).

candidates.name: Curriculum learning across garment families
candidates.training_data_requirements: Per-family difficulty ordering (use complications field in garment-families.json).
candidates.applicability_rationale: Cheap win: start with sleeveless A-line (no darts/closures), progress to darted bodice, then sleeves, then pants. Difficulty ordering already implicit in the corpus.
candidates.notes: Promote a family to next-curriculum-stage once gate-pass rate exceeds threshold (e.g. 90%).

candidates.name: MAML / Reptile (meta-learning)
candidates.training_data_requirements: Tasks across families with shared base.
candidates.applicability_rationale: Per-family LoRA + shared base achieves most of meta-learning's value at far lower complexity. Skip MAML proper.
candidates.notes: Revisit if zero-shot transfer to new families becomes a real product need.

candidates.name: DeepCAD
candidates.training_data_requirements: CAD operation sequences; we'd substitute pattern operations.
candidates.applicability_rationale: Closest prior art for predicting structured operation sequences from images/text. Architecture (transformer enc/dec over command tokens) maps directly onto our R-Model output shape.
candidates.notes: Borrow output vocabulary structure: command-id + parameter tokens, decoded autoregressively.

candidates.name: SketchGraphs
candidates.training_data_requirements: Already-published 15M parametric sketch dataset.
candidates.applicability_rationale: Useful as dataset-construction methodology rather than as a deployable model. Lesson: parametric ground truth + perturbation + retrain is a cheap, scalable training recipe.
candidates.notes: Apply the methodology to FreeSewing parameters per Source 1 in the reference doc.

candidates.name: GarmentDiffusion
candidates.training_data_requirements: Edge-tokenized garment patterns; license unclear for product use.
candidates.applicability_rationale: Too large to deploy directly; viable as a server-side teacher for distilling a smaller student we then RL-fine-tune on the gate.
candidates.notes: Their edge-token vocabulary is a natural target representation for our V-Model output too.

candidates.name: AlphaTensor / FunSearch (verifier-guided neural search)
candidates.training_data_requirements: Verifier (we have one); program/operation vocabulary (we have one).
candidates.applicability_rationale: Closest non-LLM prior art for our setup: model proposes discrete artifacts, fast verifier scores them, policy updates on verified-good. FunSearch's evolutionary recipe is directly portable.
candidates.notes: Maintain a population of pattern-program candidates; evolve under gate-derived fitness.

candidates.name: CodeRL / AlphaCode
candidates.training_data_requirements: Code generation with execution-test reward.
candidates.applicability_rationale: Our setup IS code-with-execution-feedback, where 'code' is an operation sequence and 'execution feedback' is the gate. Direct precedent.
candidates.notes: Borrow training-loop shape; clustering many candidates and picking representatives is the AlphaCode lesson.

candidates.name: ONNX Runtime Web
candidates.training_data_requirements: n/a
candidates.applicability_rationale: Stable, multi-backend (WebGPU/WebGL/WASM-SIMD), permissive license. Recommended runtime for the V-Model (encoder + Set Transformer decoder).
candidates.notes: Pair with onnx export from PyTorch.

candidates.name: transformers.js
candidates.training_data_requirements: n/a
candidates.applicability_rationale: Best ergonomics if base checkpoints are on HuggingFace; wraps ORT-Web underneath. Use if the V-Model base is HF-hosted.
candidates.notes: Slight overhead vs raw ORT-Web; usually worth it for HF interop.

candidates.name: WebLLM (MLC)
candidates.training_data_requirements: n/a
candidates.applicability_rationale: Strongest browser-LLM runtime today. WebGPU-only. Recommended for the R-Model.
candidates.notes: Falls back to wllama / llama.cpp WASM if WebGPU unavailable.

candidates.name: wllama (llama.cpp WASM)
candidates.training_data_requirements: n/a
candidates.applicability_rationale: WASM-only fallback when WebGPU is missing; ~3-4x slower than WebLLM but works on all browsers.
candidates.notes: Same GGUF format as llama.cpp; trivial portability.

candidates.name: Candle WASM
candidates.training_data_requirements: n/a
candidates.applicability_rationale: Rust-native ML; smaller bundle than ORT in some shapes but less mature for our model classes today.
candidates.notes: Track maturity; maybe revisit at v1.

candidates.name: WebNN (W3C draft)
candidates.training_data_requirements: n/a
candidates.applicability_rationale: Not deployable yet (Chrome behind flag, Safari not yet). Track for v1; could collapse the runtime stack later.
candidates.notes: Expect mainstream availability 2026-27.

v0_2.v_model: Skip the V-Model itself; ship the heuristic interpreter against the gate. Begin logging the IntelligenceLearningLoop corrections immediately. Land the operation-DAG provenance fields and validation gate hookups so future model insertion is plug-in.
v0_2.r_model: Skip the R-Model itself; ship the heuristic generator (existing FreeSewing/Bella drafter). Same plug-in readiness on operation provenance and gate.
v0_2.infrastructure: Stand up evaluation harness with calibration fixtures; benchmark spike for SmolLM2-135M / Qwen2.5-0.5B in WebLLM.

v0_5.v_model: Set Transformer (4 layer / 128 dim / 4 heads) on top of a frozen MobileSAM image encoder; per-family LoRA adapters; INT8 ONNX deployment via ORT-Web with WebGPU. Trained with supervised distillation from synthetic-from-FreeSewing labels and (consent permitting) multimodal-LLM-distilled real labels. DPO over the IntelligenceLearningLoop correction corpus.
v0_5.r_model: SmolLM2-135M-instruct (or Qwen2.5-0.5B-instruct) base + per-family QLoRA. Best-of-N=4 inference inside an iterative refinement loop, scored by the real gate. Trained supervised on synthetic perturbation->fix trajectories from FreeSewing.
v0_5.infrastructure: ORT-Web (V-Model), WebLLM (R-Model). Reward shaping with -Sigma weight_i * normalized_error_i + bonus_pass; initial weights 1 across rules.

v1.v_model: Replace MobileSAM trunk with task-distilled encoder. GRPO fine-tune on the gate. Best-of-N=8.
v1.r_model: GRPO on the gate. Best-of-N=8. Curriculum across garment families. Self-play perturbation generator.
v1.infrastructure: Evaluate distilled GarmentDiffusion student as next-gen base. Reward weights tuned with patternmaker review.

v1_5.v_model: MuZero-shape value head + beam search if accuracy plateaus.
v1_5.r_model: MuZero-shape value head + tree search; depth-3 lookahead.
v1_5.infrastructure: Migrate to WebNN if mainstream by then.

known_gaps: Browser inference benchmarks for SmolLM2-135M / Qwen2.5-0.5B on Pattern-Lab-shape prompts are extrapolated from WebLLM demos, not measured on the project's prompt format. Benchmark spike required before committing to base size.
LoRA rank choice (8 vs 16 vs 32) is workload-dependent and unresolved. Default rank 16 with v0.5 measurement spike.

Per-rule reward weights are placeholders. The six v0.1 validation rules give six numeric error signals, but correct relative weighting is a patternmaker question. Depends on Orrery design review finding 15.

Synthetic perturbation distribution for R-Model trajectory generation is unaudited. Too-small perturbations teach nothing; too-large produce uncoverable trajectories. Calibration spike required before v0.5 training.

V-Model 'image features pooled along curve' inductive bias is reasonable but unspecified at the implementation level (sample count, pooling shape, dim). Small experiment required before locking architecture.
Low-end mobile memory pressure is unmeasured. 85MB combined download is fine on desktop; mobile session retention is unknown.
Operation-kind enumeration is partially documented; the R-Model prompt vocabulary depends on it. Both should be specified together.

Consent / training-data IP for the IntelligenceLearningLoop is named but not designed (per Orrery review finding 18). Real-image distillation and DPO over user corrections both require this before shipping to actual users.
Confidence-threshold calibration for heuristic-vs-model arbitration requires a held-out evaluation set that does not yet exist. Build the evaluation harness before either model ships in production.
GarmentCodeData and SewFactory licenses are mixed/research; product training-set adoption requires legal review not yet done.
Gemma 3 270M license terms (Gemma terms) are permissive but not OSI-Apache; legal review required before adoption in shipped product.
